#!/bin/bash 
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=EQ_POCG_60
#flux: -q cmain

# The job requests 96 tasks distributed across 3 nodes.
# This results in 32 tasks per node.
#flux: -N 3
#flux: -n 96

#flux: -t 00:30:00

# The original script had multiple output directives. The last one is used.
#flux: --output=starting.out

# The '--export=ALL' and '--requeue' directives are the default or standard behavior in Flux and do not require specific flags.

# CRITICAL: The Slurm memory request '--mem=6000' (6GB total for the job) was not translated.
# Flux does not have a standard equivalent directive. The job will receive the default memory allocation,
# which will be significantly less than the requested amount and will likely cause the job to fail.
# #SBATCH --mem=6000

module purge
module load gcc cuda mvapich2/2.2

NAMD="/projects/jdb252_1/tj227/bin/namd2-2.13-gcc-mvapich2"

# 'srun' is replaced with 'flux run'. It will launch the 96 tasks requested.
# The --mpi=pmi2 flag is specific to Slurm's srun and is not needed for Flux.
flux run $NAMD starting.POCG_60.namd > starting.POCG_60.log

issues: CRITICAL: As noted in the script's comments, the original Slurm request for 6GB of total job memory (`--mem=6000`) was omitted. The job will receive a default, much smaller memory allocation and is almost certain to fail at runtime due to insufficient memory. The requested 6GB for 96 tasks is also an extremely small amount per task (~62MB), which may be an error in the original script.

The script uses two different methods for output redirection: the `#flux: --output=starting.out` directive and a shell redirection `> starting.POCG_60.log` on the `flux run` command. The output of the `flux run` command will go to `starting.POCG_60.log`, while the job's main stdout (if any other commands produced output) would go to `starting.out`. This is likely not the intended behavior and can make debugging difficult.
The path to the `namd2` executable is hardcoded to a user's project directory, which makes the script non-portable and difficult for others to use.

#!/bin/bash 
#SBATCH -J EQ_POCG_60
#SBATCH -o out%j.amarel.log
#SBATCH --export=ALL
#SBATCH --partition=cmain
#SBATCH -N 3 -n 96
##SBATCH -N 1 -n 32
#SBATCH --mem=6000
#SBATCH -t 00:30:00       # max time
#SBATCH --output=starting.out     # STDOUT output file
#SBATCH --requeue
module purge
module load gcc cuda mvapich2/2.2
NAMD="/projects/jdb252_1/tj227/bin/namd2-2.13-gcc-mvapich2"
SRUN="srun --mpi=pmi2"
$SRUN $NAMD starting.POCG_60.namd > starting.POCG_60.log
